flawed_step: 0188-0190, specifically the conclusion at 0198. The condition Tor_0(C)=Tor_1(C)^⊥ and the resulting correct cardinality do not imply that C is self-orthogonal, hence do not imply self-duality. Line 0198 checks inner products only against codewords of the form 2w, not all pairs of codewords.
counterexample: Work over Z_4 and let C be the length-2 linear code generated by (1,1): C={(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)}. Its binary torsion codes are Tor_0(C)={(0,0),(1,1)} (the residues modulo 2 of codewords) and Tor_1(C)={(0,0),(1,1)} (since 2(1,1)=(2,2) is in C, while (2,0) and (0,2) are not). The binary code {(0,0),(1,1)} is its own dual, so Tor_0(C)=Tor_1(C)^⊥ exactly as hypothesized. Nevertheless, [(1,1),(1,1)]_4=1+1=2 mod 4, so C is not even self-orthogonal. Explicitly, C^⊥={(0,0),(1,3),(2,2),(3,1)}≠C. Thus the theorem and the inference 'Hence the code is self-dual' are false.
assessment_summary: Verification stops at the first definite failure. The torsion-code criterion asserted in lines 0188-0190 is false; the explicit length-2 Z_4 code above satisfies its hypothesis but is not self-dual.
